findings.reason: the plan already specifies the advisory as one carry behind the dispatch, so the helper spread is an implementation artifact the plan's text does not mandate and a single refactor closes it without altering the design.
findings.text: the advisory is spread across seven shallow helpers — `_lane_advisory_lane` (3602), `_lane_advisory_costs` (3613), `_lane_advisory_cheaper_lane` (3695), `_lane_advisory_ledger_runs` (3770), `_lane_advisory_horizon_seconds` (3786), `_lane_advisory_instant` (3797) and `_dispatch_lane_advisory` (3805) — none of which is the interface a reader or a test faces; the behaviour they jointly hide (cost derivation, horizon comparison, lane naming, the quiet/emitted/unknown states) is one decision and would be deeper behind a single module boundary named by that decision.

findings.reason: the plan should require the clause be read through `routing_surface()` rather than re-derived, so the advisory cannot diverge from the routing figure a coordinator sees.
findings.text: §6 requires the cheaper-lane clause be "derived from the routing figures at the time of dispatch", but `_lane_advisory_costs` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3613`) forks that derivation, re-implementing rework detection and the charged median through the private helpers `capabilities_module._routing_outcome_exclusion` (3636), `_write_paths` (3658), `_paths_overlap` (3653), `_input_tokens` (3656), `_coordinator_input_tokens` (3657), `_median_or_none` (3675) and `_charged_cost` (3687) instead of consuming the public `routing_surface()` owner at `reckon/capabilities.py:892`; a private-helper fork drifts from the routing view a caller reads the moment any one of those helpers changes, which is the exact drift the plan's own comment claims the carry avoids.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the advisory the plan describes as one carry is implemented as seven small `_lane_advisory_*` helpers over the same lane machinery in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, which adds surface without adding depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 requires the cheaper-lane clause to be "derived from the routing figures", but the landed derivation re-implements rework-charged cost per durable node by reaching into private helpers of `reckon/capabilities.py` rather than extending the public owner `routing_surface()`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §7 states the plan "adds no new command and no new tool" and explains why nothing can be retired (the advisory rides a call already being made and draws its shared-window count from a directory that already exists), which is the account the item requires.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the mechanisms it extends rather than inventing: the dispatch payload and its single lane reading, the pre-flight's projected exhaustion, the gate-enforcement advisory mode, the coordinator directory (`reckon/crew/directory.py:105`, which §4 cites as "the join already exists"), and the ledger routing figures.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 justifies why the advisory cannot be an extension of the pre-flight ("the pre-flight cannot satisfy the requirement that the advisory arrive unasked, because it has to be invoked…"), so its landed shape is recorded where it will be read.
